questions.q_en:

I said to Raj," For how long have you been waiting for me?'
options_en: I asked Raj how long had he been waiting for me.
I asked Raj for how long had he been waiting for me.
I asked Raj if how long had he been waiting for me.
I asked Raj how long he was waiting for me.
questions.solution_en:
"

The correct answer is option 2)

This is an interrogative sentence.

The following changes are to be made to change it into Indirect speech:

Said to changes into told.

Comma and inverted commas are removed. A conjunction 'that' is not needed. For how long will be used as a conjunction instead. Second person pronouns in the direct speech change according to the object(Raj) of the reporting verb(said to) in the indirect speech. 'You' becomes 'he'. The tense changes from 'have been waiting'(present) to 'had been waiting'(past). An interrogative sentence beginning with question words such as how, why etc. does not need any conjunction. The question word is used as a conjunction.

"

questions.q_en:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Identify the options that arrange the part in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.

A. It took two days

B. who had set out

C. spotted by one of his

D. for him to be

E. fellow fishermen

F. to search for him
questions.solution_en:
In all the options, A is the first part, and F is the last part. Only phrase D can follow A. The preposition 'for' connects the purpose of those two days. 'To be' is followed by a participle verb. Therefore, only C can follow D because 'spotted' here will be the past participle. 'His' is a possessive determiner which requires a noun after it. So, the phrase 'fellow fisherman' can follow C. The relative pronoun 'who' refers to the subject of the sentence/clause (living things). So, B follows E. The correct order is ADCEBF.

Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

The correct sentence is: It took two days for him to be spotted by one of his fellow fishermen who had set out to search for him.

Note:

"Participle: A word formed from a verb (e.g. going, gone, being, been) and used as an adjective (e.g. working woman, burnt toast) or a noun (e.g. good breeding). In English, participles are also used to make compound verb forms (e.g. is going, has been). Consider the sentences given below:

Dancing at the party, the women fell on the ground.

Encouraged by her parents, Rita went on to pursue her passion.

The highlighted word in the first sentence is of the form Verb + ing and is used as a present participle. It is used to denote an action that is going on or incomplete or imperfect.

The highlighted word in the second sentence is of the form verb + ed. It is used as a past participle. It denotes the completed action or state of the thing spoken of.

A past participle ends with the following: -ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n.

One should take great care and never get confused between a gerund and a present participle. They use the same forms but perform different functions: a gerund is a verbal noun, while a present participle is a verbal adjective."

Possessive Determiners/Adjectives: Words like 'my', 'our', 'your', 'his', 'her', 'its', and 'their' are known as possessive adjectives (or possessive determiners). They come before nouns and indicate ownership of the noun. Example: "The teacher asked the students to open their drawing books."

Relative pronouns: A relative pronoun is used to connect a clause or phrase to a noun or pronoun. The clause modifies, or describes, the noun. The most common relative pronouns are who, whom, whose, which, and that. For example: She is the girl who received the award for bravery from our Home Minister.

For example:

Ravi said to me, Is she studying? (Direct Speech)

Ravi asked me if she was studying. (Indirect Speech)

Also, the sentence in the Direct Speech is in the tense. So, the tense in the Indirect Speech should be in the tense.

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

‘I’ changes into ‘he’ and ‘my’ into ‘his’. Change ‘said to’ into ‘asked’." ‘Can’ should be changed into ‘could’. ‘said to’ into ‘asked’ and ‘If’

Therefore, the correct answer is option (c).

questions.q_en:
Select the grammatically correct statement from among the given options.

A. He read a interesting book. The book was on history.

B. He read an interesting book. A book was on history.

C. He read an interesting book. The book was on history.

D. He read a interesting book. A book was on history.
questions.solution_en:
Option A: Incorrect.

'A interesting' is incorrect because "interesting" begins with a vowel sound and requires 'an' as "an" is used before vowel-sounding words, while "a" is used before consonant-sounding words. The second sentence is correct, but cannot compensate for the first error.

Option B: Incorrect.

The first sentence is correct with 'an interesting', but the second sentence uses 'A book', which is inappropriate here. 'The book' (using the definite article "the") should be used to refer to the specific book mentioned earlier.

Option C: Correct.

Both sentences are correct. 'An interesting book' uses the correct article for a word beginning with a vowel sound, and 'the book' appropriately refers to the specific book previously mentioned.

Option D: Incorrect.

'A interesting' is incorrect for the same reason as in Option A. The second sentence is also incorrect, as it uses 'A book' instead of 'The book'.

Hence, option (d) is the answer.

Note: Definite and indefinite articles: In the English language, we have one definite article 'the'; it refers to or introduces a particular, specific noun. 'An' and 'a' are indefinite articles; they refer to, or introduce, an unspecified noun.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

The jet almost destroyed the US aircraft. But the government doesn't give an explanation.
options_en: The US aircraft almost destroyed by the jet. But an explanation isn't given by the government.
The US aircraft was almost destroyed by the jet. But an explanation wasn't given by the government.
The US aircraft has been almost destroyed by the jet. But an explanation wasn't given by the government.
The US aircraft was almost destroyed by the jet. But an explanation isn't given by the government.
questions.solution_en:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive Voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a "to be" form of the verb is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

In Passive Voice, the preposition "by" is used before the object. However, it is optional in some cases.

The Active voice in this question is in Past Simple and Present Indefinite, respectively. Thus, the Passive voice will also be in Past Simple and Present Indefinite, respectively.

The format of Active voice is: Subject + V2 or V1/V5 + Object.

Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + was/were or am/is/are + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case).

For example:

She likes you. (Active Voice)

You are liked by her. (Passive Voice)

The options except (d) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is: The US aircraft was almost destroyed by the jet. But an explanation isn't given by the government.

questions.q_en:
Select the correct direct form of the given sentence.

Shravan said that the prisoner had slept throughout the journey.
options_en: Shravan said, "The prisoner sleeps throughout the journey."
Shravan said, "The prisoner had been sleeping throughout the journey."
Shravan says, "The prisoner has slept throughout the journey."
Shravan said, "The prisoner had slept throughout the journey."
questions.solution_en:
The sentence in the Indirect Speech is in Past Perfect Tense.

There are three cases when the Indirect Speech is in Past Perfect Tense.

Tense remains same

Past perfect changes to Present Perfect

Past perfect changes to Simple Past

Case 1: Past Perfect (Subject + had + V3 + Object) tense will be kept intact.

For example:

He said that he had just finished the movie. (Indirect Speech)

He said, "I had just finished the movie" (Direct Speech)

Case 2: Past Perfect (Subject + had + V3 +Object) will be converted into Present Perfect (Subject + has/have + V3 +Object).

For example:

He said that he had got a new job. (Indirect Speech)

He said, "I have got a new job." (Direct Speech)

Case 3: Past Perfect (Subject + had + V3 + Object) will be converted into Past Simple (Subject + V2 + Object).

For example:

He said that Arya had sent him a book. (Indirect Speech)

He said, "Arya sent me a book" (Direct Speech)

The following things in the sentence will change when changed from Indirect Speech to Direct Speech:

· Inverted commas are added, and 'that' is removed.

The reporting verb 'said' will remain as such in the direct form. Options (a), (b) and (c) are incorrect according to the change in tense. The first case is applicable here.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Shravan said, "The prisoner had slept throughout the journey."

Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. As the tide moves in and out along the shoreline, the organisms in these areas undergo drastic changes in temperature, moisture, and salinity levels within short intervals.

B. Intertidal zones, which occur along various coastlines across the globe, are unique areas that remain submerged during high tide and become exposed at low tide.

C. This dynamic and challenging environment supports a diverse range of species that have evolved to cope with rapid and extreme fluctuations in their surroundings.

D. Crabs, mussels, barnacles, and sea stars are just a few examples of the many inhabitants that possess specialized adaptations to endure this ever-changing habitat.
questions.solution_en:
The correct sequence is BCAD. Sentence B introduces the topic by clearly explaining what intertidal zones are, making it the appropriate starting point. Sentence C naturally follows by elaborating on the unique biodiversity supported by such zones. Sentence A provides a deeper insight into the environmental challenges these organisms face daily. Sentence D then concludes by giving concrete examples of creatures that live in these conditions and how they survive. This structure builds logically from definition, to explanation, to challenges, and finally to examples.

Hence, option (b) is the answer.

questions.q_en:
Select the grammatically correct sentence.

A. I need to do homework before going out to meet my friends.

B. I need to have homework before going out to meet my friends.

C. I need to done homework before going out to meet my friends.

D. I need to do homework before going out to meet mine friends.
questions.solution_en:
Sentence A correctly uses the phrase "do homework" and is grammatically correct. The phrase "do homework" is appropriate for expressing the need to complete tasks. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

B- The phrase "have homework" suggests possessing or being assigned homework, rather than completing it, which is incorrect meaningfully.

C- The phrase "to done" is incorrect. The correct form should be "to do", as the infinitive marker "to" should be followed by the base verb ['Done' is V2/V3].

D- The possessive pronoun "mine" is used without a following noun. Here, since the noun follows it, it should be replaced with "my" (possessive determiner).

Note: Possessive Determiners/Adjectives: Words like 'my', 'our', 'your', 'his', 'her', 'its', and 'their' are known as possessive adjectives (or possessive determiners). They come before nouns and indicate ownership of the noun. Example: "The teacher asked the students to open their drawing books."

Possessive Pronouns: The pronouns mine, yours, hers, his, ours, and theirs are known as possessive pronouns: they refer to something owned by the speaker or by someone or something previously mentioned. For example: The pen is mine.

Infinitive marker: A word or affix attached to the stem of a verb in order to form the full infinitive. In English, to is the infinitive marker.

questions.q_en:
The following sentence has been split into three segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If the sentence is error-free, mark 'No error' as your answer.

Each student have to come up with a new idea for the vacation activity.
questions.solution_en:
'Each' is a distributive pronoun, i.e., pronouns that consider or refer to persons or things individually or one at a time and not collectively.

So, the subject is singular which is incorrectly followed by the plural verb 'have' and this leads to an error in subject-verb agreement. It should be changed with the singular verb 'has'.

The correct sentence is: Each student has to come up with a new idea for the vacation activity.

Hence, the correct answer is option (c).

Note:

Subject-Verb Agreement: Matching up singular or plural subjects with singular or plural forms of a verb is part of the process called agreement. This can be understood better by the examples given: - "She likes cooking." [singular subject and verb] -- "They like to cook vegetables." [plural subject and verb]

questions.q_en:
Directions [Set of 4 Questions]:Read the given passage and answer the questions that follow.

The World Health Organisation (WHO) says these antibiotic-resistant "superbug infections" pose a major "global threat" to public health. Such resistance directly caused 1.27 million deaths worldwide in 2019, according to The Lancet, a medical journal. The toll is projected to rise to 10 million deaths per year by 2050, says the WHO. Antibiotics - which are considered to be the first line of defence against severe infections - did not work in most of these cases. India has the highest rate of human antibiotic use in the world. Antibiotic-resistant neonatal infections alone are responsible for the deaths of nearly 60,000 newborns each year. Researchers say the use of antibiotics was exacerbated during the Covid-19 pandemic. The weeks-long Kumbh Mela occurs in four Indian cities. The pilgrims take a holy dip in the river waters on the banks of the cities where the festival is held. The US-based researchers gathered data from some 70,000 patients who turned up at more than 40 clinics at two editions of the festival in 2013 and 2015 held in the cities of Prayagraj - also known as Allahabad - and Nashik.

More than 100 million pilgrims attended the two festivals. In Prayagraj in 2013, the patients had a median age of 46 years and most of them were men. Their common symptoms included fever, cough, runny nose, muscle pain, and diarrhoea. Researchers found that more than a third of patients at the clinics were prescribed antibiotics. In Prayagraj, nearly 69% of the patients reporting upper respiratory tract infections received antibiotics at the free state-run clinics at the festival site. "This is an alarmingly high rate, given that the vast majority of upper respiratory tract infections are viral in nature," the researchers say in a recently published paper. Researchers found that entering a clinic at the Kumbh Mela for any reason carried a one-in-three likelihood of walking out with a prescription for antibiotics. If you sought help for a runny nose, the probability increased to two in three. "When antibiotics were prescribed, there appeared to be little rhyme or reason to guide their selection," the researchers said.

As per the passage, which of the following reasons has caused a global threat?
questions.solution_en:
As per the following sentence from the first paragraph, "The World Health Organisation (WHO) says these antibiotic-resistant "superbug infections" pose a major "global threat" to public health", it can be noted that the disease caused by anti-biotic superbugs is a global threat as per the WHO.

Hence, the correct answer is option (c).
